written.myAnswer: Environmental education aims to develop awareness, understanding and responsible attitudes so people can help protect and improve the environment.
Particulate matter enters the air as tiny solid particles or liquid droplets, released by sources such as fuel combustion, vehicles, industries, construction and dust.
CO is more poisonous than CO₂.
Acid rain damages leaves and trees, removes nutrients from forest soils and can weaken or kill trees, harming forest growth.
When fossil fuels burn, their sulphur forms sulphur oxides, especially SO₂. These pollute the air and can form acids that cause acid rain.
Three sources are burning fossil fuels, deforestation, and emissions from industries and vehicles.
Wind can generate electricity and power windmills used for pumping water or grinding grain.
Pesticides can poison birds directly or accumulate in their bodies when they eat contaminated insects or seeds. They can also reduce reproduction and bird populations.
CO₂ absorbs outgoing heat. An increase in its concentration strengthens the greenhouse effect, causing global warming and climate change that can disrupt ecosystems.
Greenhouse gases absorb outgoing infrared radiation and retain heat in the atmosphere. Gases that do not absorb this radiation do not significantly cause the greenhouse effect.
A catalytic converter can oxidise CO to CO₂. Proper engine maintenance and complete combustion also help reduce CO emissions.
Solar energy can be used to heat water, cook food and generate electricity.

Carbon monoxide reduces the blood’s ability to carry oxygen; sulphur and nitrogen oxides irritate the respiratory system and contribute to acid rain; particulate matter harms the lungs and reduces visibility; and hydrocarbons and nitrogen oxides help form smog. Air pollutants can also damage plants, animals and materials.

Greenhouse gases absorb outgoing heat and keep some of it in the atmosphere. An enhanced greenhouse effect warms Earth, contributing to climate change, melting ice, rising sea levels, extreme weather and harm to people and ecosystems.
The air quality index (AQI) is a numerical scale indicating how polluted the air is and the health risks associated with that air quality.
Children, older people, and people with respiratory or heart disease are high-risk groups because they are more vulnerable to air pollution and can suffer more serious health effects.
Three strategies are environmental education and public awareness, effective environmental laws and their enforcement, and sustainable practices such as using clean energy and reducing waste.
Major causes include vehicle and industrial emissions, fuel and waste burning, construction and road dust, and winter weather conditions that trap pollutants near the ground.
In hot weather, heated air rises and helps disperse pollutants, so they are less likely to remain concentrated near the ground as they do during winter conditions.
In recent years, Pakistan has experienced severe heatwaves, irregular rainfall, floods and drought conditions. These have affected people, agriculture, water resources and infrastructure.
